q-34218:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=-14 \\ -3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ -3 & 1 & 6 & -14 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-2)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+(-2){a}_{3} & =b \\ 2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+4\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=2\cdot 4\cdot (-2)=-16.$

q-74558:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
k=0.
$$

q-74560:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ 18\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -10 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-12 \\ -2{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-10 \\ -6{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & -12 \\ -2 & 7 & -10 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ -2 & 7 & -10 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & 18 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & k+24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+24.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+24\,⇒\,k=-24.
$$

q-105248:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s+3t=-2 \\ -4s-10t=5 \\ 2s+2t=0\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ -4 & -10 & 5 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=-2,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$

q-105261:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ -s+4t=-7 \\ 3s-3t=3\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -7 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-2t=3 \\ t=-2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-2t & =3 \\ s-2(-2) & =3 \\ s+4 & =3 \\ s & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=-2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b-2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot (-2)=2.$

q-34142:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 15\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 15\end{aligned}]=-3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=-3{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}-3{a}_{1} & =0 \\ 3{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

q-105291:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ \frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=-1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

q-34276:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statements I and II are false, while statement III is true.

q-105315:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ 9{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-12{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 9 & -5 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+3(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=0
$$

and, substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-3{x}_{1}+2(0)+5(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

Since ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0$, we get that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.

Therefore, statements II and III are true, while statement I is false.

$$
